ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), as amended, including sections 10, 22, 25, 30, 31, 32, 33 and 38 on customer due diligence, beneficial owner identification, PEPs and ongoing monitoring; Companies Act 1993 sections 20-23, 118-123, 189-191 and 199-200 on registration, shareholder records, registered office and annual returns; Companies (Registration of Companies) Regulations 1994; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2018; Financial Markets Authority AML/CFT guidance and Reserve Bank of New Zealand supervisory expectations. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: New Zealand Certificate of Incorporation under Companies Act 1993, section 22
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: original certificate issued by the Companies Office; notarized certified copy; New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade apostille. For non-member states: consular legalization by the destination state's embassy or consulate in New Zealand is used in lieu of the apostille. The apostille and consular legalization routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and are never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing from the New Zealand Companies Register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: certified extract issued by the Companies Office; New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade apostille. If the receiving jurisdiction is not an Apostille Convention party, consular legalization is obtained through the relevant foreign consulate in New Zealand instead of an apostille; the two methods are alternatives and are never applied in sequence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the New Zealand company's local agent and authorized signatories for trade finance and LC transactions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of NZ_LTD, executed by the chairperson and company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution by directors; notarization of signatures by a New Zealand Notary Public; apostille issued by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade for Apostille Convention destinations. For non-member states, consular legalization by the destination consulate or embassy is used independently; apostille and consular legalization are never chained together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / New Zealand Company Constitution of NZ_LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: NZ_LTD as incorporated and registered with the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy of the constitution sealed by the company; notarized by a New Zealand Notary Public; apostille by New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. For a non-Apostille destination, consular legalization is obtained through the destination state's mission in New Zealand in substitution for the apostille, not in addition to it.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued for the NZ_LTD corporate account to support Swift_LC and TT_Wire payment rails
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The relationship bank of NZ_LTD in New Zealand, to be identified upon corporate account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer's signature certified as authentic by a New Zealand Notary Public; for Apostille Convention countries the notary's certificate receives a New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade apostille. For non-member states, consular legalization before the destination consulate is the parallel exclusive route; the two routes are never combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening applies to each director, shareholder, beneficial owner, account signatory, counterparty, trader and ultimate payee. Checks are run against the UN Consolidated List, New Zealand MFAT sanctions designations, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions, United Kingdom and European Union consolidated lists where relevant, and proprietary adverse-media and PEP databases. PEP status is identified under the AML/CFT Act and covers domestic and foreign prominent public functions; enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds review, senior management approval and heightened ongoing transaction monitoring are mandatory for any PEP, sanctions hit, negative news or unexplained risk. Screening must be repeated on a real-time risk-event basis and within 24 hours before any payment instruction, letter of credit confirmation or wire transfer is released.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online company name clearance and reservation portal, Companies Register, companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The New Zealand statutory business register operates in English; English and Maori may be used in company names. Foreign-script company names must be submitted in English or Maori transliteration or an approved romanized phonetic equivalent. The name must end with the legal form 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive primary element such as a brand, geographic or family name; (2) a descriptive business activity element such as 'Dairy Commodity Trading'; (3) a liability designator using 'Limited' or 'Ltd'; and (4) where necessary, a numeric or alphanumeric unique identifier assigned by the Register to distinguish similar names. The Register rejects names that are likely to confuse, offend, imply Crown or government connection, contain restricted words without consent, or infringe intellectual property.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, request a written statement of reasons from the New Zealand Companies Office. If the defect is typographical or similarity-based, immediately refile with a revised distinctive element. Where the Office refuses on grounds of restricted or sensitive words, submit a formal reconsideration request via the Companies Office compliance channel attaching board consent, regulatory approvals, trade mark evidence, and a statutory declaration explaining the basis. Escalate to the Registrar of Companies review process; if the refusal persists, apply for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. Do not resubmit identical names without fresh grounds.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: New Zealand Companies Act 1993 requires a physical registered office in New Zealand for service of process

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), as amended; applicable sections include ss 11-22 (incorporation and company names), ss 88-90 (allotment of shares and returns), ss 151-153 (director qualifications and consents), and ss 200-202 (registered office and service of documents).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) filed electronically through the Companies Office Company Online Registration portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed by the Companies Act 1993. The company must have at least one issued share and at least one shareholder at registration, but the share or shares may be issued for nominal consideration or for consideration payable later. No blocked escrow account or mandatory capital deposit is required under New Zealand law. Non-resident ownership is unrestricted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (NZBN-IN-REGISTRATION)

WHEREAS the Subscriber Shareholders have caused the company to be incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 as a company limited by shares; and WHEREAS the Board is required to adopt the initial corporate framework for the company, including capital subscription, banking arrangements, registered office, and statutory officers;

NOW IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT
The Board accepts the share subscriptions tabled at this meeting and, acting under section 88 of the Companies Act 1993, hereby ALLOTS [●] Ordinary Shares having a par value of NZD 1.00 each to the shareholders named in the Subscription Schedule in the proportions set out in that schedule. All allotted shares are designated as fully paid. The Managing Director is directed to enter the allotment in the Share Register, prepare and issue share certificates, and file the Return of Allotment with the Registrar of Companies within the statutory period.

2. ADOPTION OF CONSTITUTION
The Board ADOPTS the written Constitution tabled as Schedule A, which shall operate as the company's internal governance contract. Every director, officer, and agent of the company is directed to comply with the Constitution, and the Board confirms that all future acts of the company shall be authorised under the Act and the Constitution.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE
The Board ADOPTS the place shown in the Application for Registration as the company's registered office in New Zealand, being [●] New Zealand, and directs that the office be accessible during ordinary business hours. The Company Secretary is authorised to receive all correspondence, statutory notices, and legal process on behalf of the company, and to notify the Registrar of any change in registered office.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS
The Board APPOINTS [●] as Managing Director, [●] as Chairperson, and [●] as Company Secretary. Each appointee has provided a signed consent to act and has confirmed eligibility under the Companies Act 1993, including compliance with the director residence requirement in section 151. The Board records that no secretary is required by law but the appointment is made for good corporate governance and statutory compliance.

5. BANKING AUTHORITY
The Board authorises the opening of domestic and foreign currency accounts with ANZ Bank New Zealand Limited or any other reputable bank selected by the directors. All banking instructions, SWIFT wires, telegraphic transfers, letters of credit, and negotiable instruments above NZD 10,000 shall require the signatures of any two authorised signatories listed in the Banking Schedule. The directors are authorised to complete know-your-customer forms, deposit funds, negotiate bank guarantees, and manage all treasury operations.

6. LICENSING AND DUTY AUTHORISATION
The Board authorises the Managing Director and Company Secretary to apply, on behalf of the company, for all statutory registrations and permits necessary for dairy commodity trading, including the NZBN, Inland Revenue tax and GST registrations, Ministry for Primary Industries dairy export registrations, municipal licences, and civil-defence fire certificates. All filings shall be made in proper legal form within the deadlines imposed by statute.

7. GOVERNANCE AND RECORDS
The Board directs that the shareholders' register, directors' interests register, share issue records, minutes, and financial records be maintained at the registered office. The Board authorises the corporate seal in the form tabled, if adopted, and grants authority to execute all ancillary documents.

RESOLVED FURTHER that the officers are empowered to execute and deliver all agreements, declarations, and filings incidental to giving effect to these resolutions.

DATED the [●] day of [●], 20[●].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name and NZBN Viability Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Company Name Approval and NZBN Registry) under MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search on the New Zealand Companies Register using the exact proposed legal name ZELVIA NZ LIMITED to confirm that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and that it ends with LIMITED or LTD as required by the Companies Act 1993. If the name contains any restricted or regulated word, submit a Name Approval application with the Registrar and provide supporting evidence such as written consent of a professional body or a statutory declaration to satisfy the risk-of-confusion test. The application must be completed with a valid email address and an address for service in New Zealand. The same portal will reserve a provisional NZBN block for the entity and flag any existing conflict before the full incorporation application is lodged.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Availability Declaration
Identity and residential address verification for each proposed director
Written consent of any approving authority if a restricted word is used in the company name
Proposed Company Constitution, if any
Copy of the exact legal name block as displayed in the Companies Register search result
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a compliance query about the proposed name, respond in writing within 10 working days with an alternative name option, statutory declarations, or consent letters. If the application is suspended, a written request for reconsideration may be filed with the Companies Office Name Approval team together with corrected evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and a lawfully appointed New Zealand notary public or authorised certifier for foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the full incorporation package before submission. The package must include signed consents of each proposed director and any secretary, the adopted constitution, a registered office address in New Zealand, and the share subscription statements. At least one director must reside in New Zealand or, alternatively, in Australia if that person is also a director of an Australian-registered company, to satisfy the Companies Act 1993 residence requirement. All statutory forms must be completed in English. For any non-resident director, provide a certified copy of the passport, proof of residential address outside or inside New Zealand, and a declaration of recent criminal or bankruptcy history. Foreign-language documents must be accompanied by certified English translations. The registered office cannot be a postal bag or mail-forwarding address.
required_dossiers: Formal consent to act as director for every proposed director
Consent to act as secretary, if a secretary is proposed
Adopted Constitution, if the company will not rely on the First Schedule
Notice of Registered Office in New Zealand
Share Subscription and Allotment Schedule
Certified passport and residential address proof for each non-resident director
Certified English translation of any non-English supporting document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office rejects the package because a consent is missing or a director is ineligible, cure the defect by obtaining a fresh signature and an updated statutory declaration, then resubmit the corrected form within the Registrar's notice period. If a foreign document is challenged, obtain an apostille from the apostille authority of the issuing jurisdiction and provide a revised certified translation by a recognised translator.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Incorporation Submission and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Company Online Registration System via verified RealMe identity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Companies Office portal using a verified RealMe account and open the Register a Company application. Enter the approved company name, the full names and residential addresses of all shareholders and directors, the proposed registered office in New Zealand, the share structure, and any adopted constitution. Answer all solvency and compliance declarations truthfully, select the 'Limited' legal suffix, and file the application electronically as a complete package. Proceed to the secure payment screen and pay the official incorporation fee in New Zealand dollars. The system will perform an automated validation check against existing registered names and statutory disqualifications. Upon successful processing, the Registrar will issue a Certificate of Incorporation and a unique 9-digit NZBN. The company is legally formed on the date and time shown on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Verified RealMe login credentials
Approved company name block from Step 1
Complete shareholder details and share division
Directors' personal information and consent confirmations
Registered office address and contact details
Payment voucher or debit-authorisation record
Adopted constitution uploaded as a PDF attachment, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned because of an inconsistency in director or shareholder data, correct the affected fields online and resubmit without an additional fee unless the original application had to be entirely withdrawn. If the Registrar suspends the file awaiting evidence, attach the requested statutory declarations or consents within the grace period. A formal notice of refusal may be appealed by judicial review to the High Court of New Zealand if administrative error is established.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Tax, GST and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand via the myIR secure online portal and NZBN registration integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated company with Inland Revenue to obtain an IRD number and to establish the tax status of the company. The Companies Office automatically sends the incorporation record to Inland Revenue, but the company must confirm and activate the IRD account through myIR. Register for GST if the projected annual taxable supplies exceed the NZD 60,000 threshold, or elect voluntary registration if zero-rated export sales of whole and skim milk powder are expected. Apply for an employer schedule and PAYE account if any staff are to be hired, and register for KiwiSaver employer obligations. Maintain contemporaneous records of export sales, freight documentation, bills of lading, and bank payment flows to support any zero-rating of GST. Complete the entity's AML/CFT risk assessment and capture beneficial ownership details of the parent shareholder, as required by New Zealand's anti-money laundering regime.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Directors' personal IRD information if available
Bank account details of the trading bank opened or to be opened in New Zealand
Projected revenue and GST registration worksheet
Export sales or supply agreements for diary powder
AML/CFT risk assessment and beneficial ownership register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue issues a substantiation request for zero-rated exports, provide the export entry, shipping bill, and final destination certificate. If no GST return has been filed and a late notice is received, file an immediate disclosure with a reasonable-cause explanation and request remission of penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ministry for Primary Industries Dairy Export Operator and Food Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) and New Zealand Food Safety (NZFS) Registration and Assurance Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the Ministry for Primary Industries for registration as a dairy export operator under the Animal Products Act 1999 and as a registered food business under the Food Act 2014, because the company will trade in whole and skim milk powder. Use the MPI E-Cert and online assurance portal to register the product lines, warehouse premises, and loading facilities. Submit a Food Safety Programme or a Risk Management Programme statement describing receiving, storage, handling, sampling, traceability, and dispatch. The company must also identify the destination market for each consignment and comply with the applicable Overseas Market Access Requirement (OMAR) issued by the importing country. Provide a site plan, sanitation procedures, temperature control documentation, and the chain of custody for raw milk powder imports or purchases. MPI will schedule a verification inspection of the premises before final registration is confirmed and before the first export certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: MPI dairy export operator registration application
Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Food Safety Programme or Risk Management Programme summary
Warehouse floor plan and storage operating procedures
Product specification sheets for whole and skim milk powder
Traceability and supplier chain-of-custody documentation
Destination-country OMAR requirement checklist
Full exporter KYC dossier for each counterparty using Swift LC or TT Wire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MPI places the registration on hold pending inspection, submit a corrective action plan with lab test results, revised sanitation protocols, and updated temperature logs. If registration is declined for non-compliance, the company may request a reconsideration from MPI and, after exhausting internal review, appeal to the District Court under the legislation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Premises, Civil Defence and Municipal Trade Licence Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Territorial Local Authority (e.g. Auckland Council or Palmerston North City Council), Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), and WorkSafe New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company will maintain a warehouse, office, or any physical storage facility in New Zealand, secure all site-related approvals before commencing operations. Submit a building consent application to the territorial authority for any tenant fit-out, fire-separation, or cold-chain alteration. After construction is completed, obtain a Code Compliance Certificate under the Building Act 2004. Engage a chartered structural engineer to verify that the floor slab is capable of supporting concentrated loads of palletised whole and skim milk powder. Obtain a fire evacuation plan approval and a performance-based fire certificate from Fire and Emergency New Zealand under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Register the business with WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, complete a general risk assessment, and produce a worker induction record. If ammonia refrigeration or cold storage is used, obtain a Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act compliance certificate.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or certificate of title for the registered operational premises
Building Consent and Code Compliance Certificate under the Building Act 2004
Structural floor-loading certificate from a chartered engineer
FENZ fire safety inspection certificate and approved evacuation plan
WorkSafe New Zealand registration and health and safety policies
HSNO location certificate if hazardous substances or refrigerants are used
Waste disposal and washdown water discharge consent from the Regional Council
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the building certificate is queried for structural non-compliance, engage a registered engineer to issue a producer statement and apply for an amendment to the building consent. If FENZ requires additional fire protection, install the compliant alarm and suppression system and schedule a follow-up inspection. If WorkSafe identifies a risk-control deficiency, submit a health and safety improvement plan and retrain workers before operations resume.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) New Zealand Food Safety and the territorial local authority Building/Environmental Health Unit
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Dairy Export Operator Registration under the Animal Products Act 1999; Registered Food Business under the Food Act 2014; municipal food store and warehouse trade licence; and FENZ fire safety certification for any physical storage or distribution centre

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Primary Industries – New Zealand Food Safety (MPI/NZFS) in co-ordination with Environmental Protection Authority (EPA NZ) and the Regional Council under the Resource Management Act 1991 (RMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Permitted Activity (No Full EIA Report) for pure dairy commodity trading and non-processing storage. A resource consent may become a Restricted Discretionary Activity if the warehouse installs ammonia refrigeration, discharges washdown water to land or water, or stores combustible milk powder in volumes that trigger HSNO or regional plan thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source discharge is expected under the permitted trading model. Where washdown or storage generates trade wastewater, the discharge must generally remain within pH 6.0-9.0, BOD5 not exceeding 500 mg/L, COD not exceeding 1000 mg/L, and total suspended solids not exceeding 600 mg/L, unless a stricter Regional Council trade-waste bylaw applies. Airborne milk-powder dust must be kept below the New Zealand Workplace Exposure Standard of 10 mg/m3 for inhalable particulates and below 25% of the lower explosive limit of milk powder dust in any storage atmosphere. All solid dairy waste must be disposed of under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 through an approved collector, and any ammonia refrigerant system must be certified under the HSNO Act 1996.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Mandatory Fire Safety Certificate and site inspection approval from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, including fire alarm, evacuation signage, spill containment, and combustible dust housekeeping. A Building Code Compliance Certificate is required for floor-loading structural adequacy and means-of-escape compliance. WorkSafe New Zealand health and safety registration and a general risk assessment are mandatory before workers enter any warehouse. If cold-chain refrigeration is present, an HSNO location compliance certificate and annual inspection records are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Te Tari Taake, New Zealand; online filing and registration portal: myIR (myIR.ird.govt.nz); company incorporation and NZBN via New Zealand Companies Office (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the NZ_LTD domestic company: (1) Incorporate the company under the Companies Act 1993 at the New Zealand Companies Office and obtain the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); (2) IRD issues the company IRD number upon incorporation via Companies Office electronic data interchange; if not issued, the director registers the company with IRD in myIR using the company details; (3) Once the IRD number is received, log in to myIR to register for GST, PAYE, and any relevant levies. For a foreign non-resident company: (1) Confirm the company has an NZ tax nexus (carrying on business in NZ, deriving NZ-sourced income, having a fixed establishment, or making supplies to NZ consumers that trigger GST); (2) Obtain an IRD number by submitting the Inland Revenue form IR596, Non-resident company IRD number application, together with certified copies of the overseas certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles or constitution, board resolution, register of directors and shareholders, a New Zealand address for service, and, if applicable, an authorised New Zealand tax agent or agent appointment; (3) If the foreign company is required to register as an overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office, complete that filing first and include the overseas company registration number on IR596; (4) IRD assesses the residency status and registers the company; no statutory TIN fee applies; (5) Upon receipt of the IRD number, register for GST in myIR and file returns, noting that the IRD number is the taxpayer identifier for all tax types including GST. All non-English documentation must be provided in certified English translation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Eligible closely held New Zealand companies may elect look-through company (LTC) status under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, making profits transparent for members while preserving limited liability; GST-registered companies may elect GST grouping under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; a supplier below the NZD 60,000 registration threshold may voluntarily elect to register for GST. New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime and has no separate hybrid-mismatch election; hybrid mismatch rules apply as mandatory provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax Act 1985), a value-added tax administered by IRD
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period for supplies made in NZ and for remote services supplied by offshore suppliers to NZ resident consumers; once the threshold is met or exceeded, registration is mandatory under sections 51 and 54B of the GST Act 1985, with a statutory right to claim input tax from the effective date of registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no real-time tax clearance, API pre-clearance, or anti-fraud digital stamping mandate. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the IRD-approved Peppol BIS 3.0 network for interoperability; government agencies are required to accept e-invoices. GST-registered suppliers must issue GST tax invoices meeting sections 24-24E of the GST Act 1985, retain these records in New Zealand to establish time of supply, and file periodic GST returns and payments via myIR. There is no statutory requirement to transmit invoice-level data to IRD before or at invoice issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Section 11(1) of the GST Act 1985 zero-rates the supply if the goods are exported by the supplier (or by a carrier at the supplier's direction) and the supplier holds appropriate evidence that the goods have been physically removed from New Zealand; where the export is not completed before the time of supply, the goods must leave New Zealand no later than 28 days after the time of supply. For qualifying services supplied by a NZ supplier to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, zero-rating is available under section 11(1)(m) unless the services are supplied directly in connection with NZ land or physically performed in NZ. For a raw milk powder commodity seller, the sale is zero-rated as a supply of exported goods only if legal title and risk transfer are consistent with the trade terms, the goods are shipped by the NZ_LTD to a foreign buyer, an NZ Customs export declaration is accepted, and evidence of departure is retained in the GST record.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service export entry in the Trade Single Window (electronic export declaration) showing the NZ exporter of record, HS code, quantity, FOB/invoice value, and proof that Customs clearance was granted for physical departure from New Zealand

Original negotiable bill of lading or sea/air waybill evidencing loading at a NZ port/airport, foreign discharge destination, dated shipping date, and consignee outside New Zealand; the 28-day export deadline must be visible in the shipment date
Commercial invoice and packing list cross-referenced to the GST invoice, IRD number, and export entry reference, with incoterms and Peppol or EDIFACT reference where applicable
Container gate-out or terminal receipt, Customs cargo report, or overseas port arrival document proving the goods were not diverted for domestic sale

Bank-issued SWIFT MT103, TT credit advice, or documentary credit utilisation advice from a New Zealand registered bank, evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency; no New Zealand FIRC exists because New Zealand does not operate exchange controls

If the dairy product is regulated, Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) registration and clearance documents, the exporter's MPI dairy exporter registration, and any official assurance certificate required for the destination market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD requires the exporter to retain full export evidence for each zero-rated supply and will disallow the zero-rating if any statutory condition is not met, re-assessing GST at 15% on the full supply price. The unextinguished GST becomes a tax shortfall plus use-of-money interest from the original GST due date. Tax Administration Act 1994 shortfall penalties apply: 20% for failure to take reasonable care, 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 50% for an abusive tax position, and 100% for evasion, with available reductions of up to 75% for prompt voluntary disclosure. The statutory assessment time-bar is four years from the filing date, with no time bar where evasion or fraud exists. Additionally, false export declarations to NZ Customs can be prosecuted under the Customs and Excise Act 2018 and dishonesty offences under the Crimes Act 1961. New Zealand does not impose exchange-control repatriation deadlines; the critical statutory deadline for export zero-rating is that goods must be physically exported or delivered to a carrier for export within 28 days after the time of supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised current and capital account framework under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the Foreign Investment Regime. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible with no exchange control restrictions, no surrender requirements, and no prior approval for current account transactions or capital movements. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, and proceeds from the liquidation of investments may be repatriated without restriction, subject only to the standard company law solvency test and tax clearance from Inland Revenue for non-resident withholding tax on dividends and royalties. Anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 apply to all reporting entities, meaning banks require full evidentiary transparency but do not impose FX surrender or conversion ratios. The only practical hurdles are documentary in nature: banks need to verify the underlying trade, beneficial ownership, and source of funds to satisfy due diligence. Capital account transactions, such as intercompany loans or equity injections, are reportable for balance-of-payments statistics but not subject to permission. Therefore, the jurisdiction poses minimal FX regulatory friction for a dairy commodity trading entity, provided the entity maintains proper tax residency, commercial substance, and audited financial records.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender requirements or mandatory conversion timelines for export foreign currency receipts in New Zealand. Exporters may retain proceeds in NZD or any freely convertible foreign currency, hold them in offshore or onshore accounts, and repatriate them at their own discretion, subject only to bank AML/CFT screening and the reporting of transactions above NZD 10,000 for suspicious matter reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (electronic money institution) accounts are not prohibited by New Zealand law, but their viability is constrained. A New Zealand-incorporated limited company may open an account with a non-resident EMI only if the EMI holds a valid license in its own jurisdiction and the service provider is not a New Zealand reporting entity. However, a dairy commodity trader of raw milk powder requires full banking services: trade finance instruments (documentary letters of credit), SWIFT MT103 wires, and FX hedging. Offshore EMIs generally cannot issue or confirm commercial LCs, cannot provide NZD settlement through the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) operated by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, and may not be recognised as an eligible bank by foreign counterparties or New Zealand clearing systems. Furthermore, most credible EMIs are reluctant to service a physically delinked trading entity without a local banking relationship, due to correspondent bank de-risking. Therefore, EMI viability is rated Low as a primary clearing rail and Medium only as a supplementary payment corridor for small operational disbursements, provided the EMI performs full KYC and maintains segregated client funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors of a New Zealand limited company must be natural persons and are not legally required to be physically present in a branch to open a corporate bank account under the AML/CFT Act, provided the bank completes a verified remote identity process. In practice, the four major banks permit remote onboarding for directors who are existing banking customers or who complete video verification with notarised certified copies of passports and proof of residential address. For a non-resident director who is not an existing customer, most banks require an in-person interview at a branch in New Zealand, or at a New Zealand embassy or consulate with the bank's relationship manager attending by secure video link, to authenticate the principal identity document. A physical in-country presence of the trading entity (leased office or contracted service provider) is strongly recommended because banks will question the commercial substance of a shell entity involved in cross-border milk powder trading. A registered office address alone is not sufficient; banks will demand evidence of operational control, either through local directors, a local company secretary, or a New Zealand-based trust administrator with a documented service agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from layered trust structures above the NZ limited company, with unnamed discretionary beneficiaries and a foreign protector
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full trust deed redacted only for beneficiary names to the compliance team, an organisational chart showing the 25%+ ownership and control chain, a certificate of incorporation, a registered office consent form, a director/secretary certificate from the New Zealand Companies Office, an independent legal opinion from a New Zealand law firm confirming the trust is not a tax evasion vehicle, and statutory declarations from the trustee and settlor identifying the source of trust assets and economic rationale for the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags identified in dairy commodity trading, including repetitive invoicing of whole milk powder at prices materially differing from Fonterra's global auction index, frequent use of third-party payers/payees, and high-volume low-margin turnover with no warehouse receipt trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed sale and purchase agreements referencing the actual weight, quality grade, and incoterm, the corresponding Fonterra GDT auction price or an independent surveyor's valuation report (e.g., SGS or Intertek), full transport documentation (bill of lading, customs export declaration from New Zealand Customs Service, and cargo insurance certificate), warehouse receipts from a licensed cold storage facility, and a reconciled invoice-payment schedule showing that all funds are routed directly between the counterparty and the entity's own bank account without pass-through accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening hits caused by the entity having a shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner who is a politically exposed person from a jurisdiction under OFAC or UN sanctions, or who shares a name with a watchlisted individual, leading to automatic freezing of the onboarding file
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an adverse media search report from a reputable screening provider (Dow Jones, Refinitiv World-Check), a certificate of non-association from the ultimate beneficial owner, a formal written explanation of the name-match or PEP status including the nature of the political position and whether the person is under active investigation, a sworn affidavit of funds origin with independent transactional records, and a risk mitigation undertaking signed by the board of directors agreeing to enhanced monitoring and quarterly transaction reviews by the bank's AML compliance unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to verify the underlying economic substance and genuine trading purpose of the NZ limited company, particularly when the entity has no employees, no physical trading floor, and relies solely on outsourced brokers in Hong Kong or Singapore for milk powder procurement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full-year business plan with projected cash flows, a master services agreement with the outsourced broker disclosing commission rates and conflict-of-interest clauses, proof of the entity's dedicated corporate bank account and separate trust account, a lease agreement for a physical office or serviced workspace in New Zealand, the employment contract of a local trade operations manager with banking signatory authority, a copy of the entity's New Zealand Goods and Services Tax (GST) registration, and btheme last two years of management accounts demonstrating real trading activity and not merely dormancy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the New Zealand limited company must be structured either as paid-up share capital or as shareholder loans with a formal loan agreement. For share capital, the subscription funds should be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the disclosing shareholder's own bank account in the same legal name as the shareholder, using payment purpose code S101 (Issuance of shares) or S301 (Inward direct investment) as recommended by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's balance of payments coding manual. The bank will require a board resolution authorising the allotment, a share register update, and confirmation that the funds are not derived from criminal activity. For capital verification under the Companies Act 1993, the company must file an annual return with the New Zealand Companies Office, and the bank's opening deposit must match the authorised share capital. If the injection exceeds NZD 15 million, the transaction may be subject to screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 if the investor is an overseas person acquiring significant business assets, but standard trading entity capitalisation below that threshold is unrestricted. Foreign currency wires must specify the counterparty bank's BIC, the NZ bank's SWIFT code (e.g., ANZBNZ22, ASBBNZ2A), and the purpose code to avoid delays.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for raw milk powder purchases should be settled primarily through SWIFT MT103 direct wire transfers for open account transactions, with documentary collections and irrevocable confirmed letters of credit (L/C) used for larger contracts or counterparties in higher-risk jurisdictions. For New Zealand-sourced whole milk powder exports, the documentary chain typically requires the NZ exporter to present a commercial invoice, bill of lading, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, and a weight and quality certificate issued by an independent third-party surveyor. The NZ entity, as importer or re-exporter, must ensure that the destination country's bank can receive SWIFT messages and that the L/C is issued by a bank with an acceptable correspondent relationship to the NZ bank. Same-day New Zealand dollar clearing occurs through the ESAS system, but cross-border NZD/CNY or NZD/USD settlement requires the NZ bank to maintain nostro accounts in the correspondent currency, and the disbursement should be instructed before 2:00 PM NZST to meet same-day window. If the supplier demands an L/C, the NZ bank will require the underlying trade contract, an application for the L/C, and a margin deposit (typically 10-30% depending on creditworthiness). The L/C should be issued as irrevocable, available by negotiation at sight, subject to UCP600, and should permit partial shipments and transhipment to accommodate the seaborne logistics of milk powder in containers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forwards contracts on NZD/USD, NZD/CNY, and NZD/EUR with maturity up to 12 months, available through the ANZ, ASB, BNZ, or Westpac dealing desks without an underlying trade requirement if deemed a prudent treasury hedge

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the NZD against a restricted or less liquid currency where a deliverable market is not available, permitted only if the counterparty bank has an approved NDF framework and the hedge is evidenced against a future contractual cashflow

Cross-currency swaps for converting NZD-denominated debt into the operating currency (e.g., USD or CNY) to match the invoicing currency of the dairy supply contract, subject to a natural hedge test and execution under ISDA 2002 master agreement

At-the-money and collar options on NZD/USD for protecting profit margins on future milk powder sales, permissible only when the nominal exposure does not exceed 150% of the projected annual sales volume and the bank has conducted a suitability assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return to the Companies Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation (the annual return date), filing due within 30 working days after that anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of NZD 100 (approximately USD 60.00) if filed after the due date. Failure to file annual returns for three consecutive years exposes the company to administrative strike-off by the Registrar under the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Company Income Tax Return (IR 4) and payment of assessed income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March tax year, the return and final income tax payment are due by 7 July; a tax agent extension permits filing and payment by 7 September. Non-standard balance dates use the corresponding statutory filing anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing penalty of NZD 50 may be imposed. Late payment penalties accrue as an immediate 1% penalty, a further 4% penalty after 7 days, and 1% per month thereafter, capping at 10% of the unpaid amount; IRD use-of-money interest is charged daily at the prevailing prescribed underpayment rate. Persistent default may lead to IRD recovery and winding-up action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Goods and Services Tax (GST) returns and GST payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For each monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly taxable period assigned by IRD, the GST return and payment are due by the 28th day of the month following the end of the taxable period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 per return may apply; late payment penalties are the same IRD regime: 1% immediately, 4% after 7 days, and 1% per month up to a maximum 10%, with use-of-money interest running until cleared.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Fringe Benefit Tax (FBT) annual return (IR 413), if the employer provides fringe benefits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March tax year, the annual FBT return is due by 20 July following the end of the tax year; non-standard balance dates follow the corresponding statutory FBT return anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalties apply under the same IRD regime, with 1% immediate, 4% after 7 days, and 1% monthly up to 10%; late filing penalties and use-of-money interest accrue until payment and filing are completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and auditor's report for large companies (if the statutory audit threshold is met)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be completed within 5 months after balance date and signed; copies are to be delivered to shareholders within 5 working days after signature; if the company qualifies as a large filing company, audited financial statements must be filed with the Companies Office under the Registrar's financial-filing rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offences under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993 may result in director-level fines of up to NZD 10,000 and continuing default penalties of NZD 500 per day; prolonged non-compliance can lead to registration enforcement and strike-off action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent certified audit is mandatory when the company is a large company: total assets exceed NZD 60 million; or total annual revenue exceeds NZD 30 million; or it has 50 or more full-time equivalent employees. The same consolidated group metrics are applied where applicable. A company is also compulsorily audited if it is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, if it is an overseas company carrying on business in New Zealand and passes any large-company threshold, or if its constitution or a shareholder resolution validly requires an audit; medium and small companies are not statutorily audited unless one of those special triggers applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand GAAP: Tier 1 for-profit entities and FMC reporting entities must apply NZ IFRS (equivalent to IFRS as issued by the IASB); Tier 2 entities may apply the NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR). Financial statements for tax purposes must reconcile to the return under the Tax Administration Act 1994, while the External Reporting Board's XRB A1 framework is the authoritative source for applicable accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently maintain a separate beneficial-ownership register or annual UBO confirmation filing. The annual Companies Office return, however, requires the company to confirm its current directors and shareholders. Any allotment of shares must be filed with the Companies Office within 10 working days; each share transfer must be lodged with the board and the register of members updated within 10 working days of notification. AML/CFT reporting entities engaged in this commodity trading business must maintain beneficial-ownership identification records as part of customer due diligence, but these are retained internally rather than filed as a statutory annual UBO return.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand has no general tax holiday or free-zone regime. Eligible taxpayers may access the R&D Tax Incentive, a 15% refundable credit on qualifying R&D expenditure. Loss carry-forward is available indefinitely under New Zealand tax law subject to 49% shareholder continuity and business continuity tests; the 5-year figure in this payload is the schema-enforced reporting constant, not a statutory expiry.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR Form IR4 (Company Income Tax Return), filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR secure portal, with supporting schedules for imputation, transfer pricing, and foreign tax credits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due on 7 July following the balance date. For non-standard balance dates, the return is generally due by the last day of the fourth month after balance date, unless IRD grants an extension. Residual income tax is paid under provisional tax instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, IRD number, balance date, registered office, and tax residence status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm NZ tax residence via incorporation. For NZ_LTD, non-resident ownership does not alter entity-level taxation, but the return must identify ultimate beneficial owners and any non-resident directors. A PE-file must be considered if management or substantive decision-making occurs outside NZ for a non-resident business, but a NZ-incorporated company remains resident unless treaty tie-breaker rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from all sources, including gross sales revenue from raw milk powder, whole milk powder, and skimmed milk powder commodity trading.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A NZ-resident company must declare worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders are not taxed on the company's worldwide income unless dividends are distributed. Include all dairy commodity sales, trading commissions, freight recoupments, and hedging gains. Recharacterisation risk applies if invoicing routes artificially shift profits away from NZ.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest, dividend, and foreign investment fund income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose foreign dividends and interest separately. NZ_LTD must attribute controlled foreign company (CFC) income or FIF income if it holds offshore affiliates. Non-resident shareholders receiving NZ dividends are subject to non-resident withholding tax later, not at this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: cost of goods sold, freight, cold-chain logistics, insurance, broker fees, and all operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the OECD arm's length standard to all cross-border related-party purchases of milk powder or logistics services. Under New Zealand's transfer pricing rules, related-party pricing must be adjusted to arm's length. Unsubstantiated invoices from non-resident related parties trigger shortfall penalties and possible criminal liability.

Use IRD-approved tax depreciation rates. Goodwill is non-amortisable. If a non-resident affiliate owns the brand, and NZ_LTD pays a royalty for a trade mark, the royalty must satisfy transfer pricing substance and beneficial ownership tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward and net loss for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss continuity must be tested on the first day of the income year. A 49% shareholder continuity test applies; if more than 51% of direct/indirect beneficial ownership changes, tax losses lapse. Non-resident ownership changes are scrutinised with the same continuity rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the base for 28% corporate income tax. If NZ_LTD shows persistent losses for more than three consecutive years while generating third-party dairy trade revenue, IRD may examine economic substance, transfer pricing, and the general anti-avoidance rule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: R&D tax credit, imputation credits received on dividends, foreign income tax credits, and exemptions claimed under a double tax treaty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claiming a foreign tax credit requires substantiation of foreign tax paid. R&D credits require contemporaneous documentation. Treaty-exempt income must trace to a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement; failure to substantiate exposes NZ_LTD to shortfall penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit account (ICA) balance at year end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Keep an ICA record of NZ tax paid. Fully imputed dividends paid to non-residents attract a 15% NRWT rate in many DTA contexts; unimputed dividends attract a 30% statutory NRWT rate. A debit balance in the ICA creates liability under the Income Tax Act 2007.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: International related-party dealings declaration: loans, interest, royalties, goods purchases, and services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all transactions with non-resident related parties. If aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZD 10 million, a Local File must be prepared; Master File and CbCR also apply if the ultimate parent group revenue exceeds EUR 750 million. Non-disclosure is treated as non-cooperation for penalty mitigation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax paid and residual income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: NZ_LTD is generally required to pay provisional tax in three instalments if residual income tax exceeds NZD 5,000. Non-resident directors cannot be used to avoid provisional tax obligations. Unpaid tax accrues use-of-money interest from the first day after the due date.

A director must certify the return is true and correct. Knowingly signing a false return engages criminal liability under the Tax Administration Act 1994, including imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to NZD 50,000. Non-resident directors are subject to the same criminal sanctions if personally involved.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts IRD's late filing penalties, escalating for continued non-compliance, plus use-of-money interest on unpaid tax. Shortfall penalties range from 20% for lack of reasonable care to 150% for evasion. Knowingly providing false income tax returns is a criminal offence under sections 143A-143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, with maximum imprisonment of 5 years and a fine of up to NZD 50,000. Fraudulent suppression of milk powder trading income is classified as tax evasion and prosecuted accordingly.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory NRWT on dividends is 30%; fully imputed dividends are subject to 15% NRWT. Under most New Zealand DTAs, the rate is reduced to 15%, and often to 5% for a beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the voting power in the payer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate from its home tax authority; (2) complete the IRD's non-resident certificate/declaration procedures, including Form IR290 where IRD requires a reciprocal certificate, and (3) provide a signed beneficial ownership declaration confirming the recipient has the right to receive dividends, interest, or royalties and is not a conduit. The NZ payer may apply the reduced treaty rate before payment. If the payer has over-deducted NRWT, the non-resident must file an IRD refund claim within the statutory four-year time bar. For interest on approved securities, an approved issuer may elect to pay the 2% Approved Issuer Levy in lieu of 15% NRWT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on outbound royalties and interest is 15%. Under many New Zealand DTAs, the rate is reduced to 10%, and certain interest payments connected with approved issuer arrangements are subject to the 2% Approved Issuer Levy. Royalties paid for trade marks, technical know-how, or distribution rights over dairy products must satisfy beneficial ownership and transfer pricing substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 10,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions for goods, services, and intangibles; CbCR and Master File obligations apply to multinational groups with group revenue exceeding EUR 750,000,000. Financing arrangements must separately satisfy thin capitalisation and transfer pricing substance thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations register. Instead, substance is enforced through tax residence, PE definitions, the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1), transfer pricing provisions, and DTA beneficial ownership requirements. For NZ_LTD, Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) must actually occur in New Zealand: negotiating milk powder purchase contracts, taking delivery risk, managing quality specifications, issuing invoices, funding trade finance, and bearing freight and currency risk. A shell company that merely routes profits while decisions are made overseas will be disregarded or recharacterised.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of raw milk powder export revenue, fabrication of purchase invoices from non-resident related suppliers, inflating freight or cold-chain deductions, or shifting profits to a tax haven entity without commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sections 143A-143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994: evasion is criminally punishable by imprisonment for up to 5 years and a fine of up to NZD 50,000. The tax shortfall penalty is up to 150% of the evaded tax, plus use-of-money interest and late payment penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or direct fraudulent invoicing face personal civil liability for the company's losses and tax shortfalls under the Companies Act 1993, including reckless trading and insolvent trading provisions. Criminal prosecution can lead to jail, director disqualification, asset confiscation, and a court-imposed travel ban equivalent to blacklisting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit Repatriation Without Withholding Tax / DTA Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying out dividends, royalties, or interest to a non-resident parent or connected beneficiary without deducting NRWT, using a conduit entity to disguise dividends as service fees, or claiming a reduced treaty rate without an actual Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is personally liable to pay the unpaid NRWT plus late payment penalties. The Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes shortfall penalties up to 150% for the resulting tax shortfall. If the conduit is designed to defeat the purpose of the DTA, the arrangement is void under the general anti-avoidance rule and NRWT becomes fully payable at the 30% or 15% statutory rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable as withholding agents for the unpaid NRWT and penalties. The corporate veil is pierced where funds are paid away to shareholders while trade creditors or the Commissioner of Inland Revenue remain unpaid. Directors face civil asset restitution, disqualification, travel blacklisting, and imprisonment for up to 5 years if the non-payment is a deliberate evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance / AML Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating NZ_LTD as a pure paper entity for cross-border dairy commodity flows: no staff, no local office, no independent risk-taking, no records of negotiation, minimal substance, high-value Swift LC and TT wire flows passing through the entity, and no compliance with beneficial ownership record-keeping or anti-money laundering obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement is void for tax avoidance under Income Tax Act 2007 section BG 1, with a shortfall penalty of up to 100% under Tax Administration Act 1994 section 141D for taking a tax position with a dominant purpose of tax avoidance. Non-compliance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 attracts civil penalties, remedial orders, and suspension of the reporting entity's licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors personally liable for the company's liabilities, including unpaid tax, if the company is a mere sham or used for dishonest asset protection. Directors may be disqualified under the Companies Act 1993, asset-tracing orders may be made against non-resident directors, and criminal convictions under the Crimes Act 1961 for dishonest use of documents can result in imprisonment and permanent blacklisting from travel or business roles.
